A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same symmetry-breaking diagnostic and invariant-regression study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments in Table 1, ridge-regression simulations, and extensive diagnostic and ablation results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds controlled task-dependent evaluations, selective-augmentation experiments and broader sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1's core classifier diagnostic is unchanged. v2 adds selective augmentation using a 0.45 classifier-probability threshold (D.2.4). Direct task-dependent prediction already existed in v1 Appendix B; v2 refines it into a loss/accuracy ratio against a rotated-input control.

E1.justification: The benchmark roster, local point-cloud datasets and dipole-canonicalized QM7b scenario are retained. v2 D.2.4 adds a class-dependent MNIST rotation scenario, where only digits 3, 4 and 5 are rotated, alongside original and fully rotated variants.

E2.justification: The main Table 1 comparator set is retained. However, v1 C.9 compares the classifier with Chamfer, Hausdorff and Mean/Covar MMD on OC20; v2 drops that comparison while retaining these comparators for QM9 and rMD17.

E3.justification: v2 adds original-versus-rotated controls and relative loss/accuracy evaluation for the task-dependent diagnostic, selective-augmentation testing on 1,000 MNIST images, and joint sample-size, learning-rate and architecture sweeps (D.5). These substantially extend evaluation design; existing benchmark splits and training descriptions are largely retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test sample efficiency and hyperparameter sensitivity on MNIST/QM9, direct-metric sensitivity to canonicalizer and predictor architectures, selective augmentation, and diagnostic behavior across covariance strengths. Conversely, v1's QM9 and rMD17 moments-of-inertia analyses are removed.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 4 in v2 specify three-seed means and standard deviations where v1 reported unqualified point estimates. Table 2 reports five-seed results, and Figure 17 specifies four trials with fresh splits and detectors. v1 already included uncertainty in selected appendix analyses; the main expansion is systematic reporting for central comparisons.

E6.justification: Main benchmark estimates change extensively. For example, Table 1's QM9 heat-capacity FF/TF values change from 0.158/0.154 to 0.143/0.146 cal/mol K, reversing their point-estimate ordering in the new three-seed summaries. Task-dependent ratios, selective-augmentation and sensitivity results are added; OC20 MMD results and QM7b's ten-rotation group-averaging entries disappear.

T1.justification: v2 A.1 adds proofs of loss/gradient invariance and identical optimization trajectories under per-example group transformations. Appendix B adds a population-risk formulation, connections to distributional distances, and a Rademacher-complexity generalization bound. The original ridge-regression theory is retained; v1 Theorem 2 becoming v2 Fact 1 is principally relabeling.

C1.justification: The central diagnostic, dataset-bias and invariant-regression contributions remain. The abstract now identifies label-predictive symmetry bias as particularly relevant to equivariance's failures, and the contributions highlight the auxiliary task-dependent diagnostic. The conclusion narrows the salient augmentation failure from MNIST and ModelNet40 to primarily ModelNet40.

C2.justification: v1 describes the task-dependent metric as largely inconclusive beyond Swiss Roll. v2 interprets controlled direct-prediction results as supporting task relevance, adds practical recommendations conditioned on distribution shift and label correlation (Figure 6), and discusses improved architectural robustness. It also qualifies molecular augmentation benefits and explicitly leaves a reliable decision threshold for future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code address and Reproducibility Statement, plus implementation settings for selective augmentation and the new simulation classifier. It removes v1's detailed empirical-MMD and kernel implementations, Algorithms 3–6, replacing them with brief descriptions. This substantially changes the available reproduction guidance, although most original training and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references on invariance and learning theory, including Lyle et al., Sriperumbudur et al., Nguyen et al. and Cohen et al. (2019), and removes the workshop-version citation. The main related-work organization and positioning against existing symmetry tests remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The task-dependent definition moves from the experiments discussion into Section 2.1, its results are rewritten and redistributed, Swiss Roll discussion moves into the appendix, and statistical comparisons are consolidated in D.10. Terminology and experimental narrative are revised throughout, constituting substantial structural editing beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds a practical flowchart, task-dependent summary table, selective-augmentation and sensitivity plots, and a QM9 results visualization. The ridge simulation figure moves into the main text and gains a diagnostic panel; other displays are relocated, expanded or simplified. Inertia and OC20 comparison figures are removed, alongside comprehensive conference-format reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central practical argument: rotated-input controls and architecture checks address v1's inconclusive task-dependent diagnostic, while seed-based uncertainty makes the main comparisons more assessable. Additional formal analysis strengthens the explanation. These gains outweigh reduced self-contained kernel implementation detail and removed OC20 comparisons, although the practical flowchart remains heuristic without a validated decision threshold.
